title: finding(react,docs): `properties` evaluates and hoists `${…}` but the unevaluated-expression diagnostic omits it, while the props-bag diagnostic recommends it
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:ui` execution seat while implementing objectui#7418 — recording, not claiming. Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

## The claim

**`properties` is a channel that evaluates `${…}`, hoists it onto the node, and renders — and the runtime diagnostic that exists to tell an author which channels work does not list it.** Two diagnostics in the same file disagree about it.

## Measured

On `origin/main` `3faaa7d0f`, through the real production renderers (`packages/components/src/renderers/**`), driven by `SchemaRenderer` with `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0` installed. Rendered DOM, not prose:

```
badge, properties: { label: "${data.status}", variant: "${…}" }
  -> "completed" as the badge's children, and bg-secondary variant classes applied.  WORKS

card, properties: { className: "${data.isPriority ? 'border-red-500' : …}" }
  -> class="rounded-lg border … border-red-500".  WORKS

badge/card, props: { … same keys … }
  -> nothing read back; node renders as if the bag were empty.  DOES NOT WORK
```

That asymmetry is by design and is already documented in code: `props` is spread as React props, `properties` is hoisted onto the node (`SchemaRenderer.tsx`, "COMPAT: Hoist 'properties' up to schema level").

## The inconsistency

The `props`-bag diagnostic tells the author to use `properties`:

> `props` is NOT hoisted onto the node — only `properties.*` is. … Write them under `properties` instead (or at node level, where the node's schema declares the key).

The unevaluated-expression diagnostic, fired for the very same node, does not:

> Channels that do evaluate and read back today: `content`, or resolve the value in the host before handing the schema to SchemaRenderer.

`properties` is missing from that enumeration although it demonstrably is such a channel. An author who hits the second message is told their only options are `content` or host-side resolution.

## Why it cost something concrete

objectui#7418 rewrote six doc sites that authored `${…}` on keys with no carriage row. Two of them — the Status Badge and Conditional Styling sections — are about `badge` and `card.className`, which carry nothing, so under the 2026-09-01 fork (B) ruling they were rewritten to literal values plus prose. `properties` would have kept both examples dynamic. It was deliberately not used, because the docs corpus teaches it nowhere (zero occurrences of the `properties` bag in all of `content/docs/`) and introducing an authoring channel is not a docs card's decision.

## The two readings, both worth a maintainer's eye

1. **The diagnostic is incomplete.** `properties` works; the message should say so, and the guide should teach it. Cheap.
2. **`properties` is a COMPAT shim on the way out**, deliberately unadvertised. Then the `props` diagnostic should stop recommending it, and the omission is correct while the recommendation is the bug.

⛔ Not folded into objectui#7418's PR either way: one adds an authoring channel to a guide, the other retires one. Both are decisions above a docs repair.
